calls.headline: Foreigners buy $547m of Egyptian debt as Wall Street slides
calls.body: Arab and foreign investors bought a net EGP 29.38bn of Egyptian government debt on Monday, about $547m, almost all of it foreign (Amwal Al Ghad, Almasraf, Elmaser). The central bank's dollar rate eased to EGP 53.61 to buy and 53.75 to sell on Tuesday morning from 53.86 on Monday. The same day the finance ministry sold EGP 23.1bn of 18-month and three-year bonds against a EGP 20bn target, at average yields of 24.75% and 24.72%, little changed (Al Taameer, Cairo24). In shares, foreigners were net buyers of EGP 60.5m (Vetogate).
calls.view: A global sell-off that sent the Nasdaq down 2.49% did not pull money out of Egypt: foreigners kept buying debt at about 25%, and Treasury yields eased, which widens the carry. That keeps the desk's view of the pound firmer than EGP 56 into the IMF review on track, at medium confidence. Banks earn on the bills either way; importers keep their October margin while the dollar stays under EGP 54.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a debt auction clears with bids below the amount offered.

calls.headline: Small caps fall 3.76% while the EGX30 holds flat
calls.line: Profit-taking after a 10% run; market value fell EGP 51.8bn.
calls.body: The EGX70 EWI fell 3.76% to 18,028.40 on Monday and the EGX100 2.88%, while the EGX30 edged up 0.02% to 52,199.80 on gains in CIB, Telecom Egypt and Eastern Company (Al Borsa, Al Raees News). Market value fell about EGP 51.8bn to EGP 4.147tn on EGP 11.1bn of share trading (Al Masdar, Youm7). Al Borsa's analyst called it profit-taking after the EGX30's roughly 10% climb from 48,000; no outlet named a single trigger.
calls.view: The small-cap index had run 7.7% in a week to Thursday on speculative buying, so a one-day fall of this size is a reset, not a turn in the market. The desk expects the blue chips to hold up better than small caps into the MSCI changes on November 30, at low confidence: there is no news behind the selling to argue either way.
calls.wrong: The EGX70 EWI closes back above 18,700, Sunday's level, before November 30.

calls.headline: Misr Life Insurance will float 15% on the EGX in December
calls.line: The state's second offering this quarter, run by EFG Hermes.
calls.body: Misr Life Insurance plans to sell 750 million existing shares, 15% of its capital, in December, subject to approval, through a private placement and a public offering at one book-built price; the shares belong to Misr Insurance Holding, owned by the Sovereign Fund of Egypt, so the company raises nothing (press release via Fintech Gate; Al Borsa, Hapi Journal). EFG Hermes is sole global coordinator. It follows Banque du Caire's listing earlier this month.
calls.view: A second state sale in a quarter tests demand at a time foreigners are buying debt more than shares; Banque du Caire closed at EGP 5.58 on Monday, down 1.6%. A well-covered book would help EFG Holding's fees and the case that the program can raise money, but each offering also draws cash from the listed market for weeks. Medium confidence that it goes ahead in December.
calls.wrong: The offering is postponed past December, or Banque du Caire closes below EGP 5.00 before it prices.

calls.headline: Telecom Egypt and Edita lead on results and index buying
calls.line: Telecom Egypt rose 5.2% to EGP 143.00, Edita 7.4% to EGP 20.66.
calls.body: Telecom Egypt rose 5.2% to EGP 143.00 on Monday, more than double its price at the start of the year, two weeks before MSCI adds it to its standard index at the November 30 close; its nine-month profit rose 44% to EGP 24.4bn. Edita rose 7.4% to EGP 20.66, the top EGX30 gainer, after third-quarter net profit rose 41.5% to EGP 938.1m on record revenue of EGP 7.3bn, up 32.9% (Daily News Egypt, Arab Finance).
calls.view: Both moves rest on figures, not tips: earnings growth of 40% or more and, for Telecom Egypt, index buying with a date. The desk keeps Telecom Egypt on track for the MSCI inclusion and food producers among its preferred sectors, at medium confidence. After a 117% gain this year, Telecom Egypt may give some back once the index funds have bought.
calls.wrong: Telecom Egypt closes below EGP 122 before November 30, or Edita falls back below EGP 18.50 before December 15.
calls.notice: Alhoria News reported that the state auditors' review of Telecom Egypt's September accounts lists reservations, including an EGP 1.48bn loss from the Ramses exchange fire; no second outlet has confirmed it, and the view does not rely on it.

calls.headline: Fertilizer stocks fall as gas for exports gets 50% dearer
calls.line: MOPCO fell 4.1% and Abu Qir 2.4% on Monday.
calls.body: MOPCO fell 4.1% to EGP 39.03 and Abu Qir 2.4% to EGP 77.10 on Monday. EnterpriseAM, citing Asharq Business, reported that seven producers agreed to pay $175m up front for 45 days of gas from November 16 at $12.75 per mmBtu, up from $8.5, in exchange for exporting their full output into early January, with supply cuts of 20–40% still in place.
calls.view: Whatever the final terms, the plants are paying more for less gas, which supports the desk's view that rationing keeps fertilizer stocks under pressure through November; MOPCO's 56% profit rise shows urea prices still cover a lot. Low confidence: Abu Qir is EGP 8 under the EGP 85 line.
calls.wrong: Abu Qir closes above EGP 85 before November 30, or full gas supply is restored.
calls.notice: The gas price and terms come from Asharq Business, citing government sources; every other outlet repeats that report, so they are not independently confirmed, and the view does not rely on them.

calls.headline: Nasdaq enters a correction as chip stocks fall 5.3% before Nvidia
calls.body: The S&P 500 lost 1.92% to 7,416.59 on Monday, the Nasdaq 2.49% to 24,509.76, more than 10% below its record, and the Dow 1.41% to 51,608.17 (BusinessToday, Bloomberg). The Philadelphia chip index fell 5.3%; Nvidia lost 4.1% to $156.14, its lowest close since July 2025, Broadcom 3.9%, Intel 7.0%, Oracle 5.0% and Alphabet 4.1%. The VIX rose 18.7% to 22.91. Nvidia reports after the close tonight, against an LSEG consensus of $109.1bn in revenue, up 91% (Briefs Finance, BusinessToday).
calls.view: The quarter itself is not the question: worries about how AI spending is financed (Fed Governor Barr put the largest AI firms' on-balance-sheet debt above $800bn by year-end) and the new export curbs will outlast one beat. Nvidia at RSI 23 is washed out, so a relief bounce is likely, but the desk expects chip and AI-spender stocks to lag steady earners through November, at medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes back above 26,000 before November 27.

calls.headline: Washington shuts the overseas route to US AI chips for Chinese firms
calls.line: Data centers in five countries now need a license for advanced Nvidia and AMD chips.
calls.body: The Commerce Department issued a rule on Monday to stop Chinese companies using advanced AI chips through overseas data centers: customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil now need a special license to buy advanced Nvidia and AMD chips, and the rule takes effect in 90 days (NBC News, The New York Times).
calls.view: It cuts into Southeast Asian sales that had been one of Nvidia's fastest-growing channels, and it lands as the company reports under an interim chief. The size is unknown, so for now it weighs on sentiment more than earnings; the desk reads it as a reason the chip sell-off can last past tonight, at low confidence.
calls.wrong: Nvidia's guidance tonight shows no hit from the rule and the chip stocks recover Monday's 5.3% loss by November 20.

calls.headline: Brent falls 3.5% to $92.44 as a surplus outweighs Hormuz
calls.line: Down 18.5% this month although Hormuz traffic is still 95% below last year.
calls.body: Brent fell about 3.5% on Monday to $92.44 a barrel, as the IEA's forecast of a fourth-quarter surplus outweighed Iran's claim that a fourth tanker hit a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz (Reuters via ET CFO; the mine claim is unconfirmed). IMF PortWatch counted 107 transits through Hormuz in the four weeks to November 8, against 2,389 a year earlier. Exxon fell 2.2% to $166.87. Treasuries rallied, the 10-year easing to 5.12% from 5.15% (US Treasury).
calls.view: With Hormuz traffic near zero and oil still falling, the market has priced the closure and is trading the surplus; that is the desk's case for Brent below $105 to November 20, still on track. Cheaper oil eases the inflation that drives Fed hike bets, which helps bonds more than energy stocks. Medium confidence.

calls.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday at $70–78 into a falling market
calls.line: A crypto contract tracking it traded about 26% above the range on Monday.
calls.body: Anthropic prices its shares on Wednesday and starts trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT, with a range of $70 to $78 a share (Yahoo Finance, The Conversation). A crypto contract tracking the stock traded at about $98.67 on Monday, roughly 26% above the top of the range.
calls.view: A strong debut would show money still wants AI at the right price and could steady the sell-off; a weak one would deepen it. Alphabet and Amazon both hold stakes, so the price also marks their holdings. Low confidence either way until the book closes.
calls.wrong: Anthropic opens below $70 on Thursday, under its range.

calls.headline: December hike odds hold above 90% before retail sales
calls.line: October retail sales at 3:30pm Cairo are forecast up 0.2%.
calls.body: Futures still price more than a 90% chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December, from 3.75–4.00% (BigGo; EnterpriseAM, citing Reuters, put it at 91%). The 2-year yield eased to 4.83% from 4.88% on Monday (US Treasury). October retail sales, due at 3:30pm Cairo, are forecast up 0.2% on the month (TradingKey).
calls.view: A hike is priced; the risk now is a half point, which PIMCO's Tiffany Wilding says has become more likely. A strong sales figure would push yields up again and hurt the same growth stocks that fell on Monday; banks gain from a steeper path. Medium confidence that the Fed hikes a quarter point on December 9.
calls.wrong: The Fed holds rates on December 9.

view.headline: Debt inflows and remittances keep the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: Foreigners bought about $547m of Egyptian debt on the day the Nasdaq slid into a correction, which says the carry trade is not being unwound by the sell-off abroad. With bonds yielding about 24.7%, record remittances and cheaper oil, the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–55 into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. The risks are a half-point Fed hike and a delay to the final IMF review.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a debt auction clears with bids below the amount offered.

news.headline: Quebecor bids C$31bn for TELUS; TELUS jumps 12.2%
news.text: Quebecor made a non-binding cash-and-stock proposal for TELUS at about a 60% premium; TELUS's chief executive called it opportunistic.

news.headline: Tyson rises 8.7% as it sees beef losses easing
news.text: Tyson's fourth-quarter GAAP operating income fell to $1m from $158m, but it said cattle supplies are improving, and the stock closed at $63.95.

news.headline: Anthropic prices Wednesday at $70–78; trades Thursday as ANT
news.text: A crypto contract tracking the stock traded at about $98.67 on Monday, roughly 26% above the top of the range.

global.finding: Brent fell 3.5% to $92.44 on Monday as the IEA's surplus forecast outweighed Hormuz attacks, and gold slipped to $3,853, near a one-year low, as rising rate bets curb demand.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel and LNG, so Brent at $92.44, down 18.5% this month, eases the import bill and inflation; the IEA's surplus forecast is why the desk's $105 line holds.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold: the 24K gram fell 0.7% to EGP 6,755 on Monday as dollar gold slipped and the pound firmed.
notes.dxy: About 103.6, near a 19-month high; the pound still firmed 11 piasters as foreigners bought Egyptian debt.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite: about $64,600 on Tuesday morning after about $2bn of crypto positions were liquidated over the weekend.

news.headline: Brent falls 3.5% to $92.44 as the IEA sees a surplus
news.text: Oil fell more than 3% on Monday and Treasury yields eased, though analysts still see a December Fed hike.

news.headline: Hormuz transits down 95.5% on a year; Suez up 2.6%
news.text: IMF PortWatch counted 107 Hormuz transits in the four weeks to November 8 against 2,389 a year earlier; Suez had 1,211 against 1,180, and Bab el-Mandeb was down 25.4%.

news.headline: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more services to Suez
news.text: Gemini's AE1, AE2 and AE3 move from the Cape route to the Suez Canal between December and January.

news.headline: Gold near a one-year low; Goldman sees two years to a record
news.text: Spot gold closed near $3,853 on Monday, its lowest since September 2025, as rising rates curb investor demand.

news.headline: Gulf bourses recover; Qatar up 2.6% despite Bahrain attacks
news.text: Qatar rose 2.6% on Monday and Dubai and Abu Dhabi 0.2%.

news.headline: Bitcoin holds near $64,600 after $2bn of liquidations
news.text: Bitcoin steadied on Tuesday morning after about $2bn of crypto positions were liquidated over the weekend.
